text:
anne: FYI p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~11:02 UTC, p99 ~1.2s (baseline ~180-200ms), p95 ~640ms. Seeing sustained tail for ~8m. :eyes:
ops-oncall: on it, pulling traces and queue depth. any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: canary deploy completed: hosted-api v1.3.2 @ 10:59 UTC
miguel: I see router queues growing on a subset of hosts - queue_depth metric up from 2 -> 18 for shard-a. 429s are minimal but latency climbs.
sam: grabbing runtime logs from those hosts. Kernel selection logs show a pattern: heuristic chose quantized kernel 'q4_gemm_v2' then immediately fell back to 'naive_matmul_fp32' for many requests. looks like kernel fallback thrash.
lee: that fallback costs ~400-600us per call at this batch size, multiplied by backlog = bad p99. any clue why the kernel chooser flipped?
jess: sequence length dist changed around the spike, a lot of mixed short+long requests from same connections -> batching heuristic created awkward batches. batching heuristics assume uniform seq len, but this mix causes oversized batches and kernel mismatch.
perf-bot: profiler snapshot (sampled at 11:03):
```
top stacks:
- runtime::dispatch_kernel (45%)
- runtime::kv_cache_lookup (22%)
- runtime::batch_coalescer::assemble (14%)
- runtime::kernel_fallback_router (10%)
```
ops-oncall: KV cache miss rate spiked too (miss_rate 4% -> 26%) on same hosts. might be cache thrash from mixed patterns / noisy tenant.
miguel: tracing shows many cache evictions around the same time. tenant-42 was responsible for a burst of long-context requests, evicting prefixes for other tenants. noisy neighbor plausible.
anne: so root causes in flight: batching heuristic creating odd batches, kernel selector flipping, and KV cache thrash from noisy tenant -> overall queue buildup. agreed?
sam: yep. Proposed mitigations: 1) temporary isolate tenant-42 routing to a separate pool, 2) force stable kernel selection to avoid fallback for a short window, 3) raise KV cache size on affected hosts or pin hot prefixes.
lee: can we do 2) safely? forcing a kernel could break correctness for some quant profiles. but we can force 'prefer_q4' and reject requests that don't match with 415 so they drop instead of thrashing.
ops-oncall: isolating tenant-42 to dedicated pool now (routing change pushed at 11:10). monitoring impact.
deploy-bot: routing rule applied to tenant-42 -> pool-dedicated-5 @ 11:10:12 UTC
anne: after isolate -> p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 260ms within 4m, p95 back to ~220ms. queue_depth on shard-a back to 3. cache miss rate falling. :thumbsup:
jess: followups: update batching heuristics to avoid coalescing widely different seq lengths in same batch, add a small hysteresis in kernel chooser to avoid flip-flopping, and KV cache eviction policy should prefer LRU with soft pinning for hot prefixes.
miguel: I'll open PRs: batching heuristic change + chooser hysteresis. sam will add a runtime flag to prefer kernel (for emergency ops).
sam: PRs and QA checklist in the thread. also adding a perf regression test that simulates mixed short+long traffic to validate heuristics.
anne: nice work. incident classified as: performance degradation due to heuristic/kernel mismatch + noisy tenant cache thrash. postmortem please include profiler snapshots and the temporary routing change.
ops-oncall: marking incident resolved at 11:24 UTC. I'll watch for recurrence.
perf-bot: scheduled follow-up perf-run: mixed_seqlen_stress daily x3 starting tomorrow.
anne: thanks team.
